import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 433

*References:*
- [Erdős Problem 433](https://www.erdosproblems.com/433)
- P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *On a linear Diophantine problem of Frobenius*,
  Acta Arithmetica 21 (1972), 399–408.
- J. Dixmier, *Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham on Frobenius' coin problem*,
  Proceedings of the AMS 109 (1990), 567–577.
-/

namespace Erdos433

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- The Frobenius number of a finite set $A$: the greatest natural number outside the
additive submonoid generated by $A$. -/
noncomputable def frobeniusNumber (A : Finset ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m | m ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure (A : Set ℕ)}

/-- The largest Frobenius number of a $k$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose
elements have greatest common divisor one. -/
noncomputable def g (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ A.card = k ∧ A.gcd id = 1 ∧
    m = frobeniusNumber A}

/-- For every fixed $k \geq 2$, Erdős and Graham conjectured that
$$g(k,n) \sim \frac{n^2}{k-1}.$$
The conjecture was proved by Dixmier [Di90]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_433 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k, 2 ≤ k →
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (g k n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((k : ℝ) - 1))) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos433

findings.description: The module bibliography (lines 26–27) gives the wrong publication details for Dixmier’s proof: “Proceedings of the AMS 109 (1990), 567–577.” The relevant article appeared in Journal of Number Theory, and its title is also quoted inaccurately. This does not affect the mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher-deposited Crossref record at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/0022-314X(90)90150-P identifies Jacques Dixmier’s “Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham concerning the problem of Frobenius,” Journal of Number Theory 34(2) (1990), 198–209.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the Dixmier reference with: J. Dixmier, “Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham concerning the problem of Frobenius,” Journal of Number Theory 34(2) (1990), 198–209, doi:10.1016/0022-314X(90)90150-P.

reformulations.difference: The maximand uses a natural-number supremum, returning 0 when A contains 1, whereas the source’s greatest unrepresentable integer is then −1. The definition also supplies default values at parameters where no admissible set exists. These conventions do not change the stated asymptotic problem.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For gcd-one sets not containing 1, the missing natural numbers have a greatest element, which is also the source’s greatest unrepresentable integer. For sets containing 1, the two values are respectively 0 and −1. Whenever 2 ≤ k < n, the admissible set {2,…,k+1} has gcd 1 and Frobenius number at least 1, so neither 0 nor −1 can affect the maximum. Thus the signed source maximum equals the natural Lean maximum for every n > k; the finite initial discrepancies disappear in the fixed-k limit. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, Review433.maximum_eq proves this equality and Review433.limit_iff proves the equivalence of the limit statements, without using erdos_433 or sorry.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found in the three declarations. The source explicitly specifies fixed k and n → ∞, and its affirmative, solved status matches answer(True) and research solved. Lean checks cover closure as nonnegative linear combinations, gcd semantics, finite maxima, boundary values, and the ratio formulation of asymptotic equivalence. The final scratch file compiles without errors or warnings; the equivalence proof has no sorry dependency. Dixmier’s full text was blocked by the publisher, but the statement and attribution are explicit on the problem page and the bibliographic correction is independently verified. The reviewed file remains identical to the committed file.
